body:
GitHub's auto-merge is sticky, and only one of the paths that withdraws
authorisation actually disarms it.

`auto-merge.yml`'s generic validation-failure path strips the tier labels and
adds `needs-review`, but never calls `gh pr merge --disable-auto`. So a PR that
was armed, then had its head updated into forbidden paths or over the tier-2
caps, keeps a live auto-merge request while carrying `needs-review`.
`tier-label-guard.yml` has the same shape: it strips an untrusted labeller's
tier label without disarming.

`finish-armed-automerges.sh` re-checks the tier label at merge time, which
covers the finisher path -- that mitigation was added for exactly this class
(its comment credits a K3 audit). Native GitHub auto-merge is not covered by
it: if the required checks later go green on their own, GitHub merges.

#1521 fixed this for the unprotected-base path only, where the refusal now
disarms explicitly. The general rule the review drew from it is the fix here:
every path that withdraws merge authorisation must also disable auto-merge,
not merely decline to grant it again.
title: withdrawing merge authorisation does not disable auto-merge
